title: Fat Houston, Tulane gigs and Dick Allen
summary: Photos, Fat Houston at Tulane, the record with Louis Dumaine, and how Allen found him.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: Do you happen to have any old picture of the Gabriel Band or any of those bands up in the

country? No, I sure have. I sure have. I had a picture of Fat Houston too. Oh, yeah. I played with him, you know. Fat the drummer. Yes. Fat Houston. We used to play at Tulane. He played on the band that I made records with too, I believe.
Well, can you tell us some more about those records with Louis Dumaine?

Oh, Louis Dumaine? No, I have not to have none, Mr. Westbrook. Go get that record that I made lately. Of course, we played after a while. You can play it again. Yes, yes. Yeah. Yeah, that record we made with Mr. Westbrook could tell you more about that than I can, because he was at Bill, what is his name, Bill Allen? I can't think of his name. I'll get your name and his name mixed up. Was it Dick Allen? Dick Allen, Dick Allen.
He's the one that wanted me to go down and see you, you know. Yes. He heard my violin playing, and so he said that you'd be tickled to death with some of us. So, he stopped in one day.
I want to see your violins and I got two here too.
I got them all out there. Good. You'll see them when you get two.
